definitions.explanation: A serif-style typeface for CJK characters, characterized by thin horizontal strokes, thicker vertical strokes, and triangular serifs. It is the standard font for printed books and formal documents in Japan.

examples.japanese: ⟦{論文|ろんぶん}→論文：03787_ronbun⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{明朝体|みんちょうたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: Papers are written in Mincho typeface.

examples.japanese: ⟦{本文|ほんぶん}→本文：13064_honbun⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{明朝体|みんちょうたい}、⟦{見出|みだ}し→見出し：04440_midashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ゴシック{体|たい}→ゴシック体：26661_goshikkutai⟧にした。
examples.english: I set the body text in Mincho and the headings in Gothic (sans-serif).

examples.english: Mincho typeface is most commonly used in Japanese newspapers and books.

notes:
Named after the {明|みん} (Ming) dynasty of China, where this style of printing typeface originated. In Japanese typography, {明朝体|みんちょうたい} is the equivalent of serif fonts in Western typography and is considered the standard for body text in formal documents, novels, and newspapers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {明朝体|みんちょうたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{印刷|いんさつ}する→印刷する：21677_insatsusuru⟧: to print in Mincho typeface
- {明朝体|みんちょうたい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦フォント→フォント：20915_fonto⟧: Mincho font
- MS{明朝|みんちょう}: MS Mincho (a common computer font)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ゴシック{体|たい}→ゴシック体：26661_goshikkutai⟧: Gothic typeface — the Japanese equivalent of sans-serif fonts, with uniform stroke width
- {教科書体|きょうかしょたい}: textbook typeface — designed to match handwritten characters, used in school materials
- {楷書体|かいしょたい}: regular script — a typeface modeled on formal handwriting
